page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8y.large is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the ARM-based Alibaba YiTian710 processor. The instance provides 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 2.75 GHz, supported by 4.0 GB of system memory, which establishes a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It incorporates a cache structure of 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 64 MB L3 cache. Cryptographic hardware acceleration is enabled via ARM AES instructions, while traditional x86 vector extensions are absent due to the underlying arm64 architecture.

Networking and storage configurations are engineered for networked cloud deployments. The instance provides a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Local storage is not provided, meaning the instance relies entirely on external network-attached block storage for persistence. The absence of local disk drives and GPUs simplifies the profile into an entry-tier ARM compute unit.

Performance benchmark metrics show average single-thread throughput across synthetic tests, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1423.0 and a stress-ng single-core result of 1814.78. Conversely, multi-core metrics fall into lower percentiles due to the two-core limit, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 2555.0 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression of 22.22 GB/sec. Memory read bandwidth on 256 MB blocks reaches 39.5 GB/sec, while write bandwidth is measured at 15.07 GB/sec. Specialized computational tests such as ray tracing and image processing show lower throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the proprietary ARM architecture delivers standard single-threaded execution at a reduced operational hardware profile compared to traditional x86 alternatives. Tradeoffs include low overall multi-threaded capacity, modest memory headroom, and dependence on remote storage. Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8y.large is primarily fitted for lightweight web serving, microservices, low-throughput background tasks, software build workers targeting ARM64, and entry-level containerized microservices.
